cards.explanation: The answer is light. The writer says, "He wraps Himself in light as with a garment…" Most of us grab a jacket on the way out the door. The writer pictures God wearing light, friends. That's how great He is.

The answer is True. The writer pictures God making the clouds His chariot. Right after that, he has God walking on the wings of the wind. Clouds and wind, the whole sky is part of the picture, friends.

The answer is His messengers. The writer says God makes the winds His messengers. Flames of fire are His servants too. Even the weather has a job in this psalm, and I can't get my timer to do its one job.

The answer is above the mountains. The writer says God covered the earth with the deep like a garment, and the waters stood above the mountains. Think about that for a second. Friends, I get nervous when the sink fills up past the rim.
The answer is False. The writer says, "At Your rebuke the waters fled…" They don't rise, they leave in a hurry. Then the mountains rise and the valleys sink to the place God assigned for them.

The answer is so they never cover the earth again. The writer says God set a boundary they cannot cross, "…that they may never again cover the earth." The line is drawn, and the water stays behind it. I wish my dough would respect a line like that.

The answer is True. God sends springs into the valleys, and they give drink to every beast of the field. The wild donkeys quench their thirst there too. Friends, the whole field gets a drink and nobody has to stand in line.
The answer is livestock. The writer says God makes the grass grow for the livestock. Then he adds crops for people to cultivate. Animals get the grass, people get the crops, and God set up both.
The answer is the LORD. The writer says the cedars of Lebanon are the ones "…that He planted…" The psalm credits God Himself, friends. That's a fine thing to hold onto.

The big picture is that God gives each creature its place. Birds nest in the cedars, the stork has the cypresses, the wild goats have the high mountains, and the rock badgers have the cliffs. Everybody has a spot, friends. I wish my kitchen drawers were this organized.

The answer is False. The writer says God brings darkness, and it becomes night, "…when all the beasts of the forest prowl." They don't settle down, they head out. The lions withdraw later, when the sun rises.

The answer is dens. The writer says when the sun rises, the young lions withdraw and lie down in their dens. Night shift is over, and they head home. Even the lions get to go home when the work's done.
The answer is wisdom. The writer says, "In wisdom You have made them all…" Every creature, from the smallest to the biggest, was made with wisdom, friends. Nothing was thrown together.
The answer is frolic. The writer says God formed Leviathan to frolic in the sea. That's the writer's picture of it, friends. Leviathan is out there playing.

The answer is food. The writer says all creatures look to God to give them their food in due season. Every one of them is waiting on Him. When God opens His hand, they're satisfied with good things (Psalm 104:28).

The answer is that they die and return to dust, and it's a heavy verse. When God hides His face, they're terrified. When He takes away their breath, they die and return to dust. The very next verse turns toward life: when He sends His Spirit, they are created.

The answer is created. The writer says, "When You send Your Spirit, they are created, and You renew the face of the earth." New life, and the whole earth made new. I know a thing or two about being renewed, friends.
The answer is that they smolder. The writer says, "He touches the mountains, and they smolder." Just a touch, and mountains smoke. That's how powerful the writer says He is, friends.
The answer is True. The writer says, "I will sing to the LORD all my life…" He adds that he will sing praise to his God while he has his being. That's a long set list, friends.

The reason is that he rejoices in the LORD. The writer says, "May my meditation be pleasing to Him, for I rejoice in the LORD." He doesn't bring up a record or a résumé, friends. He just says he's glad in the LORD.
